title: A Growing Body of Evidence
gist_ar: نص متخصص: العبارات الاسمية المكثّفة بتكدّس معلومات وبتخفي مين اللي بيدّعي إيه.
text:
Consider the phrase "the well-documented long-term impact of export-driven,
labour-intensive growth on deeply rooted regional inequality". Twelve words, one
head noun, and at least four claims that are not being defended.

Dense premodification is the characteristic register of the policy literature,
and its economy of expression is real. To condense that phrase into clauses would
take three sentences, and a reader who works in the field will encapsulate it
correctly without effort. Precision of a kind is achieved: the writer has
specified which impact, of which growth, on which inequality.

What is lost is the distinction between what is established and what is
asserted. "Well-documented" is a modifier, so it is not a proposition and cannot
be challenged as one. A significant proportion of the increasingly complex
apparatus of this genre works the same way. A widely held belief becomes an
adjective; a contested causal mechanism becomes a compound premodifier; and
"state-of-the-art" or "purpose-built" or "cutting-edge" arrive as description
rather than evaluation, having been evaluated by nobody in particular.

The effect compounds. Because the head noun is late, the reader assembles the
qualifications first and meets the subject already framed. The extent of the
damage is difficult to quantify — which is itself a sentence of this type, and
one I would not be able to substantiate if pressed.

There is no remedy in shorter sentences, streamlined prose being perfectly
capable of the same manoeuvre. The remedy is a reading habit: unpack the noun
phrase into the claims it contains, and ask of each which is evidence and which
is furniture. In this literature the underlying causes of disagreement are
usually sitting inside a modifier, where they cannot be cited.

questions.q: What does the writer say is lost in dense noun phrases?
questions.q_ar: إيه اللي بيضيع في العبارات الاسمية المكثّفة؟
options: Precision about which impact is meant
The distinction between what is established and what is asserted

questions.q_ar: ليه مش ممكن تعترض على 'موثّق جيدًا'؟
options: It is a modifier, not a proposition
It is always true, because a well-documented claim has by definition been verified

questions.q: What does the writer admit about his own sentence on quantifying damage?
questions.q_ar: الكاتب اعترف بإيه عن جملته عن قياس حجم الضرر؟
options: It is an example of the same construction, which he could not substantiate
It was added by an editor

questions.q: What remedy does the writer propose?
options: Writing shorter sentences, since streamlined prose cannot perform the same manoeuvre
Unpacking each noun phrase and asking which parts are evidence
